correctness.rationale: Orthogonality of 1 and z gives the exact squared phase distance; rotational invariance reduces the moduli to t=||F|| and s=|a|/t. For s<1, strict E|s+sqrt(1-s^2)Z|>s follows by taking the real part (the imaginary part is almost surely nonzero); strict Cauchy–Schwarz gives m(s)<1. The derivative of t/(t^2+1-2tm) has sign 1-t^2. Thus t=1 uniquely maximizes the ratio for each s<1. For the Rice formula, polar integration gives the radial density 2r exp(-r^2-2x) I_0(2sqrt(2x)r) for |Z+sqrt(2x)|, with x=s^2/[2(1-s^2)]. Integrating the power series termwise gives the mean exp(-2x) sum_k (2x)^k Gamma(k+3/2)/(k!)^2 before rescaling; this is the Bessel expression in the proof. Differentiating that expression yields the stated factor 2x I_0-(2x+1) I_1 for m''. The Riccati equation for q=I_1/I_0 and barrier b=2x/(2x+1) give a strictly positive excess 3/(2x+1)^2 at any putative first contact. Hence m lies strictly below its endpoint chord inside (0,1). The resulting optimum is attained only at s=0,t=1, i.e. a=0, |b|=1, and has value 2.9646965828533536. Non-unimodular constants, including zero, have ratio one; unimodular constants give both norms zero.

value.rationale: The constant-plus-first-mode truncation is the first nontrivial test of vacuum modulus stability and a natural calibration for any full-space inequality. The result not only provides a sharp constant but identifies a maximally displaced affine competitor (zero vacuum component, unit first mode) and excludes every coherent offset. A global benchmark of this kind is not supplied by a local singular value or by evaluating a Rayleigh mean at one challenger.
residual_risks: This is a model-space benchmark, not a claim of sharp noisy recovery or of the optimum for higher Fock truncations.
